done_when: When the latest nightly full run failed, forge next names the platforms and failing tests and gives the forge fix start command for them

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Not done. Once a fix worktree has been started, this branch returns no scheduled-run lines at all, even if the next nightly run still fails. `forge next` then stops naming the failing platforms and tests—the visibility problem this change is meant to solve. The command-level proof explicitly expects the alert to disappear after starting a fix, but does not cover a later failed run.
findings.title: Not done: When the latest nightly full run failed, forge next names the platforms and failing tests and gives the forge fix start command

findings.body:
Gain 2, Work 2, Harm 1
Raise: Not done. The full suite spans 17 matrix jobs, so a broad regression can produce more than ten failed tests. This slice replaces every test after the tenth with a count, leaving those failures unnamed in `forge next` and putting “and N more” into the generated fix's done condition. The named proof supplies only two failed tests, so it cannot catch this case.
findings.title: Not done: a nightly run with more than ten failures does not name every failing test

why: A failing nightly full run on macOS or Windows is easy to miss, and Windows stayed red for days unseen
